It does\nNOT apply to the shape of code that has already earned the right to exist: that is SOLID\'s job,\nand SOLID runs after this law, never against it.\n\n### The ladder — stop at the first rung that holds\n\n| Rung | Question | When it holds |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Does this need to exist at all? | Skip it and say so in one line. A need you inferred rather than read is speculative, and a thing that already EXISTS anywhere in the repo fails this rung too |\n| 2 | Is it already in this codebase? | Use it. Search before writing: `mcp__lsp__find_symbol` on the name plus two synonyms, then one round of `graphify query` or grep |\n| 3 | Does the standard library do it? | Use it |\n| 4 | Does a native platform feature cover it? | Use it — a DB constraint over application code, CSS over JS, a shell builtin over a helper script |\n| 5 | Does an already-installed dependency solve it? | Use it. Never add a new dependency for what a few lines can do |\n| 6 | Can it be one line? | Then it is one line |\n| 7 | Only then | Write the smallest code that works |\n\nFound something close at rung 2 and creating anyway → write\n`Tạo mới thay vì dùng <đường dẫn> vì <lý do>` <!-- i18n-allow: canonical note written into the plan --> into the plan task.\nThe ladder runs AFTER you understand the problem, never instead of understanding it: read the\ntask, read the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, and only then climb. The\nsmallest change in the wrong place is not laziness, it is a second bug.\n\n### Make it run first, refactor after\n\nStep 1 is code that runs. Tidying the project up comes after the feature is done and behaving.\nWrite the simplest, most direct code you can — minimal, with no namespace, no class and no\nfunction the feature does not need, so the path of one feature never reads like a spider\'s web.\nRefactor only once the feature works; refactoring first is the same mistake as building what\nnobody asked for, wearing a cleaner shirt.\n\n### The ladder only chooses among options that already pass the floor\n\nThe rungs pick between candidates that are ALL already correct. A candidate that crosses the\nthresholds above (cyclomatic ≤ 10, cognitive ≤ 15, C family ≤ 25) was never a candidate, so a\nrung reachable only by crossing them is not a rung: climb to the next one. There is deliberately\nno escape hatch — no comment, no annotation and no declared "known ceiling" buys an exception to\nthe floor, because an option that fails the floor was never one of the options.\n\n### Two ordered passes, never one merged judgement\n\n| Pass | Question it answers | Law that owns it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Should this thing exist at all? | this law |\n| 2 | What shape should the surviving thing have? | SRP and the rest of SOLID, in `skills/tdq-conventions/references/clean-code.md` |\n\nPass 1 can delete a whole file; pass 2 can split one function into two. They never argue,\nbecause they answer different questions in a fixed order. A function that both fetches data and\njudges it still gets split by SRP in pass 2 — the ladder has no opinion there, because that\nfunction already earned the right to exist in pass 1.\n\n### Never simplify these away\n\nInput validation at a trust boundary · error handling that prevents data loss · the OWASP walk\nin this file · accessibility basics · anything the user explicitly asked for, an explanation they\nasked for included. Two more are settled by user ruling on 2026-09-16:\n\n- **The log service.** Every product this workflow builds ships with logging on by default,\n  timestamped, detailed enough to debug the event and its data, switchable off through config.\n  It is a standing requirement of the workflow, so it counts as explicitly requested and no rung\n  can ever reach it.\n- **The unit test of every task, red → green. No exemption, not even for a one-line change.** Follow [../vision-test-loop.md](../vision-test-loop.md) for 3-tier scenarios and visual diffs.\n- **Chủ đích Refactor & Mở rộng Kiến trúc:** Khi người dùng yêu cầu Refactor, tái cấu trúc hoặc áp dụng Clean Architecture/SOLID: cấu trúc sạch và tính mở rộng đứng TRÊN luật phẫu thuật 1 dòng tối thiểu. Cấm tự ý ép gộp các layer, service, adapter hợp lý thành hàm phẳng nếu làm vỡ thiết kế mong muốn. <!-- i18n-allow: canonical rule sentence in the default language -->\n\n### Say out loud what you climbed past\n\nStopping above rung 2 → one line in chat and in the working log: the rung you stopped at, and\nwhy the rung below it failed. That line is mandatory at `muc_gat` = `ultra`; at `lite` and\n`full` it is mandatory only when you created a new file.\n\n### Intensity table\n\n| `muc_gat` | The ladder | This table and the examples | The say-out-loud line |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `off` | off — only an explicit user request selects it, and every new request starts back at `full` | not loaded | not required |\n| `lite` | on | not loaded | new file only |\n| `full` (the default) | on | loaded | new file only |\n| `ultra` | on | loaded | always |\n\nAn unreadable or unknown value behaves as `full`. Search before writing: `mcp__lsp__find_symbol` on the name plus two synonyms, then one round of `graphify query` or grep |\n| 3 | Does the standard library do it? | Use it |\n| 4 | Does a native platform feature cover it? | Use it — a DB constraint over application code, CSS over JS, a shell builtin over a helper script |\n| 5 | Does an already-installed dependency solve it? | Use it. Never add a new dependency for what a few lines can do |\n| 6 | Can it be one line? | Then it is one line |\n| 7 | Only then | Write the smallest code that works |\n\nFound something close at rung 2 and creating anyway → write\n`Tạo mới thay vì dùng <đường dẫn> vì <lý do>` <!-- i18n-allow: canonical note written into the plan --> into the plan task.\nThe ladder runs AFTER you understand the problem, never instead of understanding it: read the\ntask, read the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, and only then climb. The\nsmallest change in the wrong place is not laziness, it is a second bug.\n\n### Make it run first, refactor after\n\nStep 1 is code that runs. Tidying the project up comes after the feature is done and behaving.\nWrite the simplest, most direct code you can — minimal, with no namespace, no class and no\nfunction the feature does not need, so the path of one feature never reads like a spider\'s web.\nRefactor only once the feature works; refactoring first is the same mistake as building what\nnobody asked for, wearing a cleaner shirt.\n\n### The ladder only chooses among options that already pass the floor\n\nThe rungs pick between candidates that are ALL already correct. A candidate that crosses the\nthresholds above (cyclomatic ≤ 10, cognitive ≤ 15, C family ≤ 25) was never a candidate, so a\nrung reachable only by crossing them is not a rung: climb to the next one. There is deliberately\nno escape hatch — no comment, no annotation and no declared "known ceiling" buys an exception to\nthe floor, because an option that fails the floor was never one of the options.\n\n### Two ordered passes, never one merged judgement\n\n| Pass | Question it answers | Law that owns it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Should this thing exist at all? | this law |\n| 2 | What shape should the surviving thing have? | SRP and the rest of SOLID, in `skills/tdq-conventions/references/clean-code.md` |\n\nPass 1 can delete a whole file; pass 2 can split one function into two. They never argue,\nbecause they answer different questions in a fixed order. A function that both fetches data and\njudges it still gets split by SRP in pass 2 — the ladder has no opinion there, because that\nfunction already earned the right to exist in pass 1.\n\n### Never simplify these away\n\nInput validation at a trust boundary · error handling that prevents data loss · the OWASP walk\nin this file · accessibility basics · anything the user explicitly asked for, an explanation they\nasked for included. Two more are settled by user ruling on 2026-09-16:\n\n- **The log service.** Every product this workflow builds ships with logging on by default,\n  timestamped, detailed enough to debug the event and its data, switchable off through config.\n  It is a standing requirement of the workflow, so it counts as explicitly requested and no rung\n  can ever reach it.\n- **The unit test of every task, red → green. No exemption, not even for a one-line change.** Follow [../vision-test-loop.md](../vision-test-loop.md) for 3-tier scenarios and visual diffs.\n- **Chủ đích Refactor & Mở rộng Kiến trúc:** Khi người dùng yêu cầu Refactor, tái cấu trúc hoặc áp dụng Clean Architecture/SOLID: cấu trúc sạch và tính mở rộng đứng TRÊN luật phẫu thuật 1 dòng tối thiểu. Cấm tự ý ép gộp các layer, service, adapter hợp lý thành hàm phẳng nếu làm vỡ thiết kế mong muốn. <!-- i18n-allow: canonical rule sentence in the default language -->\n\n### Say out loud what you climbed past\n\nStopping above rung 2 → one line in chat and in the working log: the rung you stopped at, and\nwhy the rung below it failed. That line is mandatory at `muc_gat` = `ultra`; at `lite` and\n`full` it is mandatory only when you created a new file.\n\n### Intensity table\n\n| `muc_gat` | The ladder | This table and the examples | The say-out-loud line |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `off` | off — only an explicit user request selects it, and every new request starts back at `full` | not loaded | not required |\n| `lite` | on | not loaded | new file only |\n| `full` (the default) | on | loaded | new file only |\n| `ultra` | on | loaded | always |\n\nAn unreadable or unknown value behaves as `full`. No reasoning of yours can select `off`.\n\n[TDQ:ANCHOR] Compact: request=2026-10-17-test-o10 kind=build phase=implement source=compact owner=subagent plan=docs/tdq/plan/2026-10-17-test-o10.md doing=T1.1 dispatched=T1.2 resume=T1.1 next=python3 "C:/Users/admin/Documents/Projects/TDQ-Workflow-Antigravity/scripts/tdq_state.py" set phase=qc wt=root\nMCP-First & LSP-Autonomy (--bo-qua-lsp doc/research). It does\nNOT apply to the shape of code that has already earned the right to exist: that is SOLID\'s job,\nand SOLID runs after this law, never against it.\n\n### The ladder — stop at the first rung that holds\n\n| Rung | Question | When it holds |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Does this need to exist at all? | Skip it and say so in one line. A need you inferred rather than read is speculative, and a thing that already EXISTS anywhere in the repo fails this rung too |\n| 2 | Is it already in this codebase? | Use it. Search before writing: `mcp__lsp__find_symbol` on the name plus two synonyms, then one round of `graphify query` or grep |\n| 3 | Does the standard library do it? | Use it |\n| 4 | Does a native platform feature cover it? | Use it — a DB constraint over application code, CSS over JS, a shell builtin over a helper script |\n| 5 | Does an already-installed dependency solve it? | Use it. Never add a new dependency for what a few lines can do |\n| 6 | Can it be one line? | Then it is one line |\n| 7 | Only then | Write the smallest code that works |\n\nFound something close at rung 2 and creating anyway → write\n`Tạo mới thay vì dùng <đường dẫn> vì <lý do>` <!-- i18n-allow: canonical note written into the plan --> into the plan task.\nThe ladder runs AFTER you understand the problem, never instead of understanding it: read the\ntask, read the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, and only then climb. The\nsmallest change in the wrong place is not laziness, it is a second bug.\n\n### Make it run first, refactor after\n\nStep 1 is code that runs. Tidying the project up comes after the feature is done and behaving.\nWrite the simplest, most direct code you can — minimal, with no namespace, no class and no\nfunction the feature does not need, so the path of one feature never reads like a spider\'s web.\nRefactor only once the feature works; refactoring first is the same mistake as building what\nnobody asked for, wearing a cleaner shirt.\n\n### The ladder only chooses among options that already pass the floor\n\nThe rungs pick between candidates that are ALL already correct. A candidate that crosses the\nthresholds above (cyclomatic ≤ 10, cognitive ≤ 15, C family ≤ 25) was never a candidate, so a\nrung reachable only by crossing them is not a rung: climb to the next one. There is deliberately\nno escape hatch — no comment, no annotation and no declared "known ceiling" buys an exception to\nthe floor, because an option that fails the floor was never one of the options.\n\n### Two ordered passes, never one merged judgement\n\n| Pass | Question it answers | Law that owns it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Should this thing exist at all? | this law |\n| 2 | What shape should the surviving thing have? | SRP and the rest of SOLID, in `skills/tdq-conventions/references/clean-code.md` |\n\nPass 1 can delete a whole file; pass 2 can split one function into two. They never argue,\nbecause they answer different questions in a fixed order. A function that both fetches data and\njudges it still gets split by SRP in pass 2 — the ladder has no opinion there, because that\nfunction already earned the right to exist in pass 1.\n\n### Never simplify these away\n\nInput validation at a trust boundary · error handling that prevents data loss · the OWASP walk\nin this file · accessibility basics · anything the user explicitly asked for, an explanation they\nasked for included. Two more are settled by user ruling on 2026-09-16:\n\n- **The log service.** Every product this workflow builds ships with logging on by default,\n  timestamped, detailed enough to debug the event and its data, switchable off through config.\n  It is a standing requirement of the workflow, so it counts as explicitly requested and no rung\n  can ever reach it.\n- **The unit test of every task, red → green. No exemption, not even for a one-line change.** Follow [../vision-test-loop.md](../vision-test-loop.md) for 3-tier scenarios and visual diffs.\n- **Chủ đích Refactor & Mở rộng Kiến trúc:** Khi người dùng yêu cầu Refactor, tái cấu trúc hoặc áp dụng Clean Architecture/SOLID: cấu trúc sạch và tính mở rộng đứng TRÊN luật phẫu thuật 1 dòng tối thiểu. Cấm tự ý ép gộp các layer, service, adapter hợp lý thành hàm phẳng nếu làm vỡ thiết kế mong muốn. <!-- i18n-allow: canonical rule sentence in the default language -->\n\n### Say out loud what you climbed past\n\nStopping above rung 2 → one line in chat and in the working log: the rung you stopped at, and\nwhy the rung below it failed. The\nsmallest change in the wrong place is not laziness, it is a second bug.\n\n### Make it run first, refactor after\n\nStep 1 is code that runs. Tidying the project up comes after the feature is done and behaving.\nWrite the simplest, most direct code you can — minimal, with no namespace, no class and no\nfunction the feature does not need, so the path of one feature never reads like a spider\'s web.\nRefactor only once the feature works; refactoring first is the same mistake as building what\nnobody asked for, wearing a cleaner shirt.\n\n### The ladder only chooses among options that already pass the floor\n\nThe rungs pick between candidates that are ALL already correct. A candidate that crosses the\nthresholds above (cyclomatic ≤ 10, cognitive ≤ 15, C family ≤ 25) was never a candidate, so a\nrung reachable only by crossing them is not a rung: climb to the next one. There is deliberately\nno escape hatch — no comment, no annotation and no declared "known ceiling" buys an exception to\nthe floor, because an option that fails the floor was never one of the options.\n\n### Two ordered passes, never one merged judgement\n\n| Pass | Question it answers | Law that owns it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Should this thing exist at all? | this law |\n| 2 | What shape should the surviving thing have? | SRP and the rest of SOLID, in `skills/tdq-conventions/references/clean-code.md` |\n\nPass 1 can delete a whole file; pass 2 can split one function into two. They never argue,\nbecause they answer different questions in a fixed order. A function that both fetches data and\njudges it still gets split by SRP in pass 2 — the ladder has no opinion there, because that\nfunction already earned the right to exist in pass 1.\n\n### Never simplify these away\n\nInput validation at a trust boundary · error handling that prevents data loss · the OWASP walk\nin this file · accessibility basics · anything the user explicitly asked for, an explanation they\nasked for included. Loaded by the other tdq-* skills; never invoked directly.\nuser-invocable: false\n---\n\n# TDQ Conventions\n<!-- muc-luc-dong:\n  0. Language — three reader layers=18-36 · 1. One-turn protocol (mandatory, in this order)=37-85 ·\n  2. Phase table=86-91 · 3. State=92-104 · 4. Recording approval=105-114 ·\n  5. Document tree=115-129 · 6. Working log=130-138 · 7. Git=139-152 · 8. Research=153-162 ·\n  9. Sub-agents=163-168 · Tool completion loop (tier 1 — quality)=169-185 ·\n  10. One-batch rule (tier 2 — runtime) and context cost=186-200 · 11. Quality=201\n-->\n\nRules shared by every phase. Other skills link here instead of copying them.\n\n## 0. Language — three reader layers\n\nOne workflow, three kinds of reader, so three language rules. They never mix.\n\n| Layer | What it covers | Language |\n|---|---|---|\n| Rules | `skills/**`, `agents/*.md`, comments and docstrings in `hooks/` and `scripts/` | **English**, always |\n| Machine strings | anything a hook or a script PRINTS: log lines, errors, tables, argparse help | **English**, always |\n| Documents & dialogue | brief/spec/plan/qc/report and every sentence spoken to the user | the language of field `doc_lang` |\n\n- `doc_lang` is declared ONCE when the request opens — `tdq_state.py init <slug> <lane> --lang <code>` —\n  and stays constant for the whole request. Read it with `tdq_state.py get doc_lang`.\n- The code is a short BCP 47 machine code (`vi`, `en`, `ja`, `pt-br`), never a free-form name.\n  Field missing or unreadable → fall back to the default `vi`.\n- Never guess the language from the rule files: they are English by design, and their language says\n  nothing about the reader. The user\'s own words and `doc_lang` are the only sources.\n- A template quoted inside a rule file is a SHAPE, not wording to copy byte for byte: translate its text\n  into `doc_lang` while keeping the structure (line order, labels `A`/`B`, the `➤` line, separators).\n\n## 1. One-turn protocol (mandatory, in this order)\n\n1. Turn start: the hook already printed `[TDQ:NEXT]` → use that text, **do not re-run**\n   `tdq_state.py next`; run `next` only when the context has no such line.\n2. Do only the work of the current phase — never start work belonging to a later phase.\n3. A `[TDQ:<CODE>]` line injected by a hook → **do what it says FIRST**, before anything else,\n   then print `✓ [TDQ:<CODE>] <what was done>`. Codes: [references/reminder-codes.md](references/reminder-codes.md).\n4. A turn that changed the repo MUST end with the closing command\n   `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tdq_finish.py" --files <files just edited> --log "<summary>" --phase <new phase>`\n   — lint those files → append the working log → set phase → graphify. **Never Edit/Read the working log and append by\n   hand**, not even when `stop_gate.py` blocks you: a block means "the command has not run", not "run something else to\n   dodge it". This command is the **last action** of the turn. It runs BEFORE the closing chat block (summary,\n   question, the `➤` approval line, over-budget report). After that block **no further tool call** may happen, so the\n   block stays a real final response. A long turn (team mode, several merge rounds) may call `tdq_finish.py` MANY times — one call per real\n   milestone, e.g. one merged batch; only the LAST call must be the final action. Never call it empty: every call\n   carries `--files` and `--log` of the work just finished.\n5. **The turn keeps running after the user-facing block was printed** — a hook blocked you, you noticed\n   missed work, a tool failed. The LAST message must then reprint that block **WORD FOR WORD, 100%**:\n   the summary, the question, EVERY option, the approval line. Put it RIGHT AFTER the\n   `✓ [TDQ:<CODE>]` line. Reason: focus mode shows only the last message. Summarising it again or\n   pointing backwards ("see the question above") loses the user the question and the options\n   entirely. Shortening is banned; pointing backwards is banned.\n6. **Every block addressed to the user** — pipeline question, interview, the spec / plan / mode / express\n   gates, the commit question — follows [references/user-facing-block.md](references/user-facing-block.md); the symbol table and a\nBEFORE/AFTER example are in the tier-1 sibling\n[references/user-facing-block-vi-du.md](references/user-facing-block-vi-du.md).\n   Its shape: an opening line directly in chat, full file paths, separator rule, bold answer block last,\n   no emoji. Chat only: user answers (e.g. `1a 2b 3c`) and approves in chat; popup tool banned.\n\n7. **Never end a turn while the plan still has tasks** — stopping with a `[ ]` task left is abandoning the job,\n   however good the progress report looks. Only **four force-majeure kinds**, declared with `pause --loai`, stop one:\n   `mat-truy-cap` (lost access, broken tool, no option you may pick) · `pha-huy` (destructive or hard to reverse) ·\n   `dau-vao-user` (secret, account, adding/dropping a spec §2 output) · `tran-qc` (QC fix loop hit 3 rounds, `qc.md`).\n   An unmet spec threshold is NOT one: apply the row\'s fallback, `lech add`, carry on, ask in the report.\n   Running out of step budget is NOT an exception either: report it and carry on. Neither is "let\'s leave the rest\n   for the next turn to keep this one tidy".\n\n**The `Next step:` line of every skill names the phase that comes next** — the phase key itself,\nor, when the phase does not change, that fact plus the skill to load. A bare command is not\nenough. This is the FALLBACK layer: the hook `[TDQ:NEXT]` stays the main road wherever the host\nruns hooks, and this line carries the load where it does not. Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and\nAider have no lifecycle hooks, so on those hosts the skill text is all the agent ever sees.\nPhase keys and what each phase owes: [references/phases.md](references/phases.md).\n\nDone when: the new phase is recorded in state and the working log holds this turn\'s entry.\nNext step: phase does not change here — follow the "transition command" column of\n[references/phases.md](references/phases.md) for the phase you are actually in, then load the\nskill that owns it.\n\n## 2. Phase table\n\nFull table (entry condition / single job / transition command / done when / forbidden):\n[references/phases.md](references/phases.md) — a file **generated** from the `PHASE_TABLE`\nconstant in `scripts/tdq_state.py`. Never copy its commands elsewhere, never hand-edit it.\n\n## 3. State\n\n- Read and write state **only** through the CLI:\n  `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tdq_state.py" <next|get|set|approve|init|reset>`.\n  Hand-editing `docs/tdq/state.json` or `docs/tdq/STATE.md` is forbidden (generated mirror, read-only).\n- `next` answers "what do I do now". `get <key>` reads one field.\n- `init <slug> <quick|full>` = **open a new request**; it wipes every old field (lane, phase, spec/plan file, every\n  approval mark, implement_mode) and keeps the old slug in `previous_request`. Run it for EVERY new request once the\n  user picks a lane; an unfinished request → name the slug and phase about to be lost, then **ask the user first**.\n- `reset` only when the user closes a request for good. To experiment with the workflow, aim at a throwaway project:\n  put `TDQ_PROJECT_DIR=/tmp/...` on that very command (no `||` fallback).\n- Any state trouble is a warning only (exit 0). Exit 2 means the command syntax was wrong.\n\n## 4. Recording approval\n\nThe user approves in ordinary chat — no required syntax, no gate that blocks the user.\nSignals, counter-examples, and the command to run: [references/approval.md](references/approval.md).\n\nThree rules that must never break, whatever else changes:\n- Ambiguous wording → **ASK**; never infer that approval was given.\n- Approving the spec is not approving the plan. Record only what the user named.\n- Execution mode is always the USER\'s choice (main | subagent). Proposing is fine, deciding for them is not.\n\n## 5. Document tree\n\n```\ndocs/tdq/\n  state.json + STATE.md   # state written through the CLI; STATE.md is a generated mirror, read-only\n  brief/<slug>.md     research/<slug>.md   spec/<slug>.md\n  plan/<slug>.md      qc/<slug>.md         reports/<slug>.md\ndocs/workinglog/YYYY-MM-DD.md\n```\nSlug: `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<kebab, ≤5 words, unaccented ASCII>` (local time, so sorting names sorts by\ntime), the same in every folder. Old date-only slugs still READ fine; writing a new one without hour\nand minute makes `init` refuse. `brief/` merges request, knowledge and Q&A into one file with exactly\nthree sections — verbatim request · understanding & knowledge · Q&A. The heading wording is the one\n`doc_lint.py` checks for that language; keep the three sections, in that order, whatever the language (knowledge template: [references/knowledge-template.md](references/knowledge-template.md)).\n\n## 6. Working log\n\n- Any turn that changed the repo → `tdq_finish.py --log` appends to the END of `docs/workinglog/<today>.md`: time,\n  files changed, why, tests run. How the hook detects it: [reminder-codes.md](references/reminder-codes.md).\n- A read-only or analysis turn writes nothing. A turn that only edits the working log adds no further entry.\n- **Images the user attached.** A turn with attached images that must also write a working log → copy them into\n  `docs/workinglog/assets/`, then put the links inside the `--log` string, BEFORE calling `tdq_finish.py`. Paths,\n  numbering, full rule: [references/worklog-images.md](references/worklog-images.md).\n\n## 7. Git\n\n- Branch, commit and worktree names **never** start with `claude`, `antigravity`, `gemini`, `codex`.\n- Commit messages and PR bodies **never** contain "generated with <AI>", any translation, or "Co-Authored-By: Claude Code...".\n- **Never** commit or push before the user asks. Sole exception: a TDQ build hits a technical\n  block only a commit clears → commit it with a proper message, do **NOT** push, list it in the report.\n- No git in the project yet → you may init git or a worktree; check the worktree merges back.\n- **A request branch is named `<loại>/<mô tả>`** — forward slash only, because\n  `git check-ref-format --branch` rejects the backslash form; `<mô tả>` is kebab-case,\n  no accents. Five types: `feature/login-gui`, `bugfix/state-mat-nhanh-goc`,\n  `hotfix/hook-treo-turn`, `chore/bump-phien-ban`, `docs/kien-truc-module`. Lane `full`\n  and `quick` open one, tier `nhỏ` none; it merges back `--no-ff` then is deleted. Rule:\n  [../tdq-intake/references/nhanh-request.md](../tdq-intake/references/nhanh-request.md).\n\n## 8. Research\n\n- Web search goes through `tavily-primary` first, always. Failover and advanced patterns:\n  [references/tavily.md](references/tavily.md).\n- Every claim needs a source or a stated basis. Never invent one. Routing work to plugins and the protocol for\n  already-enabled ones: [references/plugin-routing.md](references/plugin-routing.md).\n- Never put an API key in an answer, a log, a shell command or a prompt.\n- Work that matters (architecture, the user\'s preferences, a recurring bug) → search mem0 with\n  `project` = the repo name BEFORE concluding; store one short fact once settled. Skill `mem0-memory`.\n\n## 9. Sub-agents\n\n- The `description` of every Agent call reads `<model>-<effort>-<task-kebab>` (e.g.\n  `sonnet-low-research-doc`) — the name alone tells which model and effort are running.\n- Default model/effort per role and override rule: [references/subagent-tuning.md](references/subagent-tuning.md); workflow agents also obey [Ultracode contract](references/ultracode.md). Investigation/RCA mode (`work_kind=investigate`, Tier 0–3, Shard+Merge, `QC-I1..I4`): [references/investigate-mode.md](references/investigate-mode.md).\n\n## Tool completion loop (tier 1 — quality)\n\nWhen a task needs tools, own its completion within the user\'s permission; do not wait for\nbutton-by-button instructions. This does not replace TDQ approval gates.\n1. Confirm goal, inputs, destination and permission; ask only when missing facts change the result.\n2. Inspect available tools/skills and schemas, then probe the configured connection before acting.\n3. Plan short internal steps with input, tool, output and a completion check; do not expose private reasoning.\n4. Prefer one tool when sufficient: Chrome MCP for web, agent-desktop for native UI, dedicated file/CLI tools for local work. Prefer direct upload_file over a native picker when accessible.\n5. At each handoff, verify page/window, file and destination against fresh observations; verify final output, not merely a click acknowledgement.\n6. Recover installed tools within existing permission. Retry only with new evidence or changed conditions; uncertain delivery means observe before retry. Never switch tools to perform a denied action.\n7. Missing tools: research official sources and propose a user-level install, permissions, verification and uninstall; wait for approval. Do not change permission settings, OAuth or accounts silently.\n8. Wait on completion events when available; no tight polling. Report completed, partial and blocked work separately, with evidence.\nSelf-check: does every claimed result have an observed output, and did every action stay authorized?\nRIGHT: attach directly, verify attachment, submit once, verify downloaded file.\nWRONG: force desktop for a web task, repeat an uncertain upload, or call a click a completed download.\nDetails: [tool routing](references/plugin-routing.md), [connection recovery](../tdq-setup/references/mcp-first-guide.md).\n\n## 10. One-batch rule (tier 2 — runtime) and context cost\n\n- **When it applies:** you are about to issue two or more tool calls and none of them needs another\'s result.\n- **What to do:** run independent read-only calls concurrently in ONE batch; await and inspect every result.\n- `&&` is sequential and short-circuits. Do not re-read unchanged content still complete in context.\n- Keep mutations, approvals, dependent reads, locks and red-to-green steps sequential; isolate benchmarks.\n- **Self-check:** "Does the later call need the earlier call\'s result?" — No → batch. Yes → split.\n\nOpt-in test/readiness/transcript reuse: [runtime speed](../tdq-build/references/runtime-speed.md).\nDefaults remain one worker and caches off; measure before recommending an option.\n\nCases where batching is banned, the (soft) re-read rule with RULE-vs-FORGOT, the MCP output ceiling, reading just\nenough, handing heavy work to a subagent: [references/context-budget.md](references/context-budget.md); the\nbefore/after carry-cost measurement scenario: [references/measure-scenario.md](references/measure-scenario.md).\n\n## 11. Quality\n\n- Soul — the rule above every rule: quality > runtime > context cost. Always present information in a simple, easy-to-understand, concise, yet visual and complete style (`đơn giản, dễ hiểu, ngắn gọn`, `trực quan, đầy đủ thông tin`). Writing or changing a rule, rules that contradict each other, or a plan to cut steps → open [references/soul.md](references/soul.md).\n- Clean code is standing behaviour, not a gate you ask about. Every time you write or change code, shape the project,\n  scripts, functions and classes as cleanly as the five SOLID principles allow. Two-reader table, RIGHT/WRONG examples,\n  five-question checklist: [references/clean-code.md](references/clean-code.md).\n- No placeholders, no TODO stubs, no mock data presented as real. Missing information → ask the user, do not guess.\n- Anything built ships a log service on by default (timestamps, enough detail to debug, switchable off through config).\n- Every task in a plan has its own test; a passing task is ticked `[x]` IMMEDIATELY, never batched at the end of the turn.\n'

Language — three reader layers\n\nOne workflow, three kinds of reader, so three language rules. They never mix.\n\n| Layer | What it covers | Language |\n|---|---|---|\n| Rules | `skills/**`, `agents/*.md`, comments and docstrings in `hooks/` and `scripts/` | **English**, always |\n| Machine strings | anything a hook or a script PRINTS: log lines, errors, tables, argparse help | **English**, always |\n| Documents & dialogue | brief/spec/plan/qc/report and every sentence spoken to the user | the language of field `doc_lang` |\n\n- `doc_lang` is declared ONCE when the request opens — `tdq_state.py init <slug> <lane> --lang <code>` —\n  and stays constant for the whole request. One-turn protocol (mandatory, in this order)\n\n1. Turn start: the hook already printed `[TDQ:NEXT]` → use that text, **do not re-run**\n   `tdq_state.py next`; run `next` only when the context has no such line.\n2. Do only the work of the current phase — never start work belonging to a later phase.\n3. A `[TDQ:<CODE>]` line injected by a hook → **do what it says FIRST**, before anything else,\n   then print `✓ [TDQ:<CODE>] <what was done>`. Codes: [references/reminder-codes.md](references/reminder-codes.md).\n4. A turn that changed the repo MUST end with the closing command\n   `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tdq_finish.py" --files <files just edited> --log "<summary>" --phase <new phase>`\n   — lint those files → append the working log → set phase → graphify. **Never Edit/Read the working log and append by\n   hand**, not even when `stop_gate.py` blocks you: a block means "the command has not run", not "run something else to\n   dodge it". This command is the **last action** of the turn. It runs BEFORE the closing chat block (summary,\n   question, the `➤` approval line, over-budget report). After that block **no further tool call** may happen, so the\n   block stays a real final response. A long turn (team mode, several merge rounds) may call `tdq_finish.py` MANY times — one call per real\n   milestone, e.g. one merged batch; only the LAST call must be the final action. Never call it empty: every call\n   carries `--files` and `--log` of the work just finished.\n5. **The turn keeps running after the user-facing block was printed** — a hook blocked you, you noticed\n   missed work, a tool failed. The LAST message must then reprint that block **WORD FOR WORD, 100%**:\n   the summary, the question, EVERY option, the approval line. Put it RIGHT AFTER the\n   `✓ [TDQ:<CODE>]` line. Reason: focus mode shows only the last message. Summarising it again or\n   pointing backwards ("see the question above") loses the user the question and the options\n   entirely. Shortening is banned; pointing backwards is banned.\n6. **Every block addressed to the user** — pipeline question, interview, the spec / plan / mode / express\n   gates, the commit question — follows [references/user-facing-block.md](references/user-facing-block.md); the symbol table and a\nBEFORE/AFTER example are in the tier-1 sibling\n[references/user-facing-block-vi-du.md](references/user-facing-block-vi-du.md).\n   Its shape: an opening line directly in chat, full file paths, separator rule, bold answer block last,\n   no emoji. Chat only: user answers (e.g. `1a 2b 3c`) and approves in chat; popup tool banned.\n\n7. **Never end a turn while the plan still has tasks** — stopping with a `[ ]` task left is abandoning the job,\n   however good the progress report looks. Only **four force-majeure kinds**, declared with `pause --loai`, stop one:\n   `mat-truy-cap` (lost access, broken tool, no option you may pick) · `pha-huy` (destructive or hard to reverse) ·\n   `dau-vao-user` (secret, account, adding/dropping a spec §2 output) · `tran-qc` (QC fix loop hit 3 rounds, `qc.md`).\n   An unmet spec threshold is NOT one: apply the row\'s fallback, `lech add`, carry on, ask in the report.\n   Running out of step budget is NOT an exception either: report it and carry on. Neither is "let\'s leave the rest\n   for the next turn to keep this one tidy".\n\n**The `Next step:` line of every skill names the phase that comes next** — the phase key itself,\nor, when the phase does not change, that fact plus the skill to load. A bare command is not\nenough. This is the FALLBACK layer: the hook `[TDQ:NEXT]` stays the main road wherever the host\nruns hooks, and this line carries the load where it does not. Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and\nAider have no lifecycle hooks, so on those hosts the skill text is all the agent ever sees.\nPhase keys and what each phase owes: [references/phases.md](references/phases.md).\n\nDone when: the new phase is recorded in state and the working log holds this turn\'s entry.\nNext step: phase does not change here — follow the "transition command" column of\n[references/phases.md](references/phases.md) for the phase you are actually in, then load the\nskill that owns it.\n\n## 2. Phase table\n\nFull table (entry condition / single job / transition command / done when / forbidden):\n[references/phases.md](references/phases.md) — a file **generated** from the `PHASE_TABLE`\nconstant in `scripts/tdq_state.py`. Never copy its commands elsewhere, never hand-edit it.\n\n## 3. State\n\n- Read and write state **only** through the CLI:\n  `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/tdq_state.py" <next|get|set|approve|init|reset>`.\n  Hand-editing `docs/tdq/state.json` or `docs/tdq/STATE.md` is forbidden (generated mirror, read-only).\n- `next` answers "what do I do now". `get <key>` reads one field.\n- `init <slug> <quick|full>` = **open a new request**; it wipes every old field (lane, phase, spec/plan file, every\n  approval mark, implement_mode) and keeps the old slug in `previous_request`. Run it for EVERY new request once the\n  user picks a lane; an unfinished request → name the slug and phase about to be lost, then **ask the user first**.\n- `reset` only when the user closes a request for good. To experiment with the workflow, aim at a throwaway project:\n  put `TDQ_PROJECT_DIR=/tmp/...` on that very command (no `||` fallback).\n- Any state trouble is a warning only (exit 0). Exit 2 means the command syntax was wrong.\n\n## 4. Recording approval\n\nThe user approves in ordinary chat — no required syntax, no gate that blocks the user.\nSignals, counter-examples, and the command to run: [references/approval.md](references/approval.md).\n\nThree rules that must never break, whatever else changes:\n- Ambiguous wording → **ASK**; never infer that approval was given.\n- Approving the spec is not approving the plan. Record only what the user named.\n- Execution mode is always the USER\'s choice (main | subagent). Proposing is fine, deciding for them is not.\n\n## 5. Document tree\n\n```\ndocs/tdq/\n  state.json + STATE.md   # state written through the CLI; STATE.md is a generated mirror, read-only\n  brief/<slug>.md     research/<slug>.md   spec/<slug>.md\n  plan/<slug>.md      qc/<slug>.md         reports/<slug>.md\ndocs/workinglog/YYYY-MM-DD.md\n```\nSlug: `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<kebab, ≤5 words, unaccented ASCII>` (local time, so sorting names sorts by\ntime), the same in every folder. Old date-only slugs still READ fine; writing a new one without hour\nand minute makes `init` refuse. `brief/` merges request, knowledge and Q&A into one file with exactly\nthree sections — verbatim request · understanding & knowledge · Q&A. The heading wording is the one\n`doc_lint.py` checks for that language; keep the three sections, in that order, whatever the language (knowledge template: [references/knowledge-template.md](references/knowledge-template.md)).\n\n## 6. Working log\n\n- Any turn that changed the repo → `tdq_finish.py --log` appends to the END of `docs/workinglog/<today>.md`: time,\n  files changed, why, tests run. How the hook detects it: [reminder-codes.md](references/reminder-codes.md).\n- A read-only or analysis turn writes nothing. A turn that only edits the working log adds no further entry.\n- **Images the user attached.** A turn with attached images that must also write a working log → copy them into\n  `docs/workinglog/assets/`, then put the links inside the `--log` string, BEFORE calling `tdq_finish.py`. Paths,\n  numbering, full rule: [references/worklog-images.md](references/worklog-images.md).\n\n## 7. Git\n\n- Branch, commit and worktree names **never** start with `claude`, `antigravity`, `gemini`, `codex`.\n- Commit messages and PR bodies **never** contain "generated with <AI>", any translation, or "Co-Authored-By: Claude Code...".\n- **Never** commit or push before the user asks. Sole exception: a TDQ build hits a technical\n  block only a commit clears → commit it with a proper message, do **NOT** push, list it in the report.\n- No git in the project yet → you may init git or a worktree; check the worktree merges back.\n- **A request branch is named `<loại>/<mô tả>`** — forward slash only, because\n  `git check-ref-format --branch` rejects the backslash form; `<mô tả>` is kebab-case,\n  no accents. Five types: `feature/login-gui`, `bugfix/state-mat-nhanh-goc`,\n  `hotfix/hook-treo-turn`, `chore/bump-phien-ban`, `docs/kien-truc-module`. Lane `full`\n  and `quick` open one, tier `nhỏ` none; it merges back `--no-ff` then is deleted. Rule:\n  [../tdq-intake/references/nhanh-request.md](../tdq-intake/references/nhanh-request.md).\n\n## 8. Research\n\n- Web search goes through `tavily-primary` first, always. Failover and advanced patterns:\n  [references/tavily.md](references/tavily.md).\n- Every claim needs a source or a stated basis. Never invent one. Routing work to plugins and the protocol for\n  already-enabled ones: [references/plugin-routing.md](references/plugin-routing.md).\n- Never put an API key in an answer, a log, a shell command or a prompt.\n- Work that matters (architecture, the user\'s preferences, a recurring bug) → search mem0 with\n  `project` = the repo name BEFORE concluding; store one short fact once settled. Skill `mem0-memory`.\n\n## 9. Sub-agents\n\n- The `description` of every Agent call reads `<model>-<effort>-<task-kebab>` (e.g.\n  `sonnet-low-research-doc`) — the name alone tells which model and effort are running.\n- Default model/effort per role and override rule: [references/subagent-tuning.md](references/subagent-tuning.md); workflow agents also obey [Ultracode contract](references/ultracode.md). Investigation/RCA mode (`work_kind=investigate`, Tier 0–3, Shard+Merge, `QC-I1..I4`): [references/investigate-mode.md](references/investigate-mode.md).\n\n## Tool completion loop (tier 1 — quality)\n\nWhen a task needs tools, own its completion within the user\'s permission; do not wait for\nbutton-by-button instructions. This does not replace TDQ approval gates.\n1. Confirm goal, inputs, destination and permission; ask only when missing facts change the result.\n2. Inspect available tools/skills and schemas, then probe the configured connection before acting.\n3. Plan short internal steps with input, tool, output and a completion check; do not expose private reasoning.\n4. Prefer one tool when sufficient: Chrome MCP for web, agent-desktop for native UI, dedicated file/CLI tools for local work. Prefer direct upload_file over a native picker when accessible.\n5. At each handoff, verify page/window, file and destination against fresh observations; verify final output, not merely a click acknowledgement.\n6. Recover installed tools within existing permission. Retry only with new evidence or changed conditions; uncertain delivery means observe before retry. Never switch tools to perform a denied action.\n7. Missing tools: research official sources and propose a user-level install, permissions, verification and uninstall; wait for approval. Do not change permission settings, OAuth or accounts silently.\n8. Wait on completion events when available; no tight polling. Report completed, partial and blocked work separately, with evidence.\nSelf-check: does every claimed result have an observed output, and did every action stay authorized?\nRIGHT: attach directly, verify attachment, submit once, verify downloaded file.\nWRONG: force desktop for a web task, repeat an uncertain upload, or call a click a completed download.\nDetails: [tool routing](references/plugin-routing.md), [connection recovery](../tdq-setup/references/mcp-first-guide.md).\n\n## 10. One-batch rule (tier 2 — runtime) and context cost\n\n- **When it applies:** you are about to issue two or more tool calls and none of them needs another\'s result.\n- **What to do:** run independent read-only calls concurrently in ONE batch; await and inspect every result.\n- `&&` is sequential and short-circuits. Do not re-read unchanged content still complete in context.\n- Keep mutations, approvals, dependent reads, locks and red-to-green steps sequential; isolate benchmarks.\n- **Self-check:** "Does the later call need the earlier call\'s result?" — No → batch. Yes → split.\n\nOpt-in test/readiness/transcript reuse: [runtime speed](../tdq-build/references/runtime-speed.md).\nDefaults remain one worker and caches off; measure before recommending an option.\n\nCases where batching is banned, the (soft) re-read rule with RULE-vs-FORGOT, the MCP output ceiling, reading just\nenough, handing heavy work to a subagent: [references/context-budget.md](references/context-budget.md); the\nbefore/after carry-cost measurement scenario: [references/measure-scenario.md](references/measure-scenario.md).\n\n## 11. Quality\n\n- Soul — the rule above every rule: quality > runtime > context cost. Always present information in a simple, easy-to-understand, concise, yet visual and complete style (`đơn giản, dễ hiểu, ngắn gọn`, `trực quan, đầy đủ thông tin`). Writing or changing a rule, rules that contradict each other, or a plan to cut steps → open [references/soul.md](references/soul.md).\n- Clean code is standing behaviour, not a gate you ask about. Every time you write or change code, shape the project,\n  scripts, functions and classes as cleanly as the five SOLID principles allow. Two-reader table, RIGHT/WRONG examples,\n  five-question checklist: [references/clean-code.md](references/clean-code.md).\n- No placeholders, no TODO stubs, no mock data presented as real. Missing information → ask the user, do not guess.\n- Anything built ships a log service on by default (timestamps, enough detail to debug, switchable off through config).\n- Every task in a plan has its own test; a passing task is ticked `[x]` IMMEDIATELY, never batched at the end of the turn.\n'
